lines.en: I accepted the book and stood there blankly for a moment before asking the butler,
“When did you say Her Majesty gave you this book?”
“Her Majesty gave me the first manuscript forty years ago. She continued to give me manuscripts regularly for another ten years or so. All I did was bind them into a book.”
“Did you read it?”
“I swear I have not read a single line. As I said, I handled only the binding and layout.”
I opened the book.
A neatly organized table of contents appeared.
Episode 13. The Princes Strike Back
Episode 14. The First Prince’s Rebellion
Episode 15. Three Methods
I flipped through the pages in a frenzy.
It was a thick volume, but with my attribute’s effects, I had little trouble reading it.
Someone, however, was unhappy with my speed-reading.
“You are reading far too quickly.”
“Maybe you’re just slow, hyung.”
“What does it say?”
I did not answer.
As I turned the pages, a strange exhaustion washed over me. The fatigue and desperation of the years, embedded in every page. I did not know whether Han Sooyoung had intended that.
One thing was certain: Han Sooyoung had known the moment would come when I read her book.
I paused where I was and opened the very last part of the volume.
There was an <Author’s Afterword>.
「Honestly, there are always people who open a book straight to the author’s afterword.」
Sentences that greeted me as if they had been waiting. Despite the circumstances, I almost laughed.
「By the time you read this book, I’ll probably be······.」
With a heavy heart, I read the next sentence.
「Still alive and kicking. Haha, scared you?」
That little shit.
「Anyway, if my prediction is right, the person reading this is Kim Dokja. Prince Kim Dokja, huh. What a shame I can’t see you like that.」
Han Sooyoung’s unmistakable sarcasm seeped through every line.

「How did I know it was you? Well······ to be honest, I’m not certain either. Even my Predictive Creation has its limits. There are just certain possibilities and cliché conditions that apply if you come to this world, and I guessed the likeliest one. Of course, I could be wrong.」
Playfully written sentences.
But what they described was no joke.
「Actually, I hope I’m wrong. Me, waiting decades for someone······ Do you think that’s possible, you lunatic?」

Han Sooyoung’s <Author’s Afterword> had not been written all at once. She had probably gathered these records little by little from the moment she possessed a body in this world, then accumulated them in writing once she could write for herself.
Her record continued.

「You’ve probably guessed, but I was born in this woman’s body. At first I thought I’d reincarnated······. For the first year or so, the frustration nearly drove me insane. If I hadn’t organized my memories using [Avatar] inside my head, I’d have lost it long ago. Things got a little better when I turned four and could write. Fucking hell, I suppose I’m a writer after all, wanting writing to save me even at a time like this.」
I did not know whether to laugh or cry. All I could do was silently turn the pages.

「At first, I thought you’d come after about three years at the latest. You came back after three years before, didn’t you? But then three years passed, then four, then five······ (Don’t assume time flew by just because I’m describing it like this.) My thinking changed. And at some point, I accepted it.」
Turning the pages grew harder.
「I see. Kim Dokja isn’t coming anytime soon.」
Han Sooyoung’s handwriting trembled faintly.
「The fucking bastard told me to wait, and he isn’t coming.」
What could I say?
「But I suppose that isn’t Kim Dokja’s fault.」
No, whatever I said, could it even reach the Han Sooyoung who had written this?
「Sorry. You probably don’t want to read this stuff either. But you know, it’s not easy to keep from whining here.」
Her sentences went on.

「I never realized this when I wrote novels, but actually living here means dealing with all sorts of inconvenient details I never imagined. The shower facilities are a pain to use, fist-sized bugs crawl around the bedroom, and the food······ Let’s not go there.」
Through the sixth year.
「You know my speech is getting weird lately? I sound like some medieval noblewoman.」
Through the seventh.
「Sir Kim Dokja. When might you grace us with your arrival?」
Through the eighth.
「Bleurgh.」
Through the ninth.
「It feels like a joke. That a human life can pass this quickly.」
After that, the records became sporadic.
The entries were not in chronological order, and here and there were records that seemed to have been added later.
「Fuck」
「Kim Dokja, you son of a bitch」
「What the hell do you expect me to do, you shitty dokkaebi bastards」
「The time I’ve lived here is starting to catch up with the time I lived on Earth.」
「······So next time we meet, call me noona. Got it?」
Han Sooyoung’s handwriting was gradually changing.
As if it were changing from Han Sooyoung’s handwriting into something no longer her own.
「Actually, I’m writing this because I have some idea of what my future will be. And maybe this world’s future, too.」
Decades might be a short time to constellations.
But not to humans.
Han Sooyoung had to endure an entire lifetime here.
「I started thinking this scenario might not appear in ‘Ways of Survival’. That would make sense. We’ve changed so many stories.」
We.
After enduring all those years alone, did you still include me in that ‘we’?
「If I sit back and do nothing too, you and Yoo Joonghyuk will obviously flail around doing stupid shit until you ruin the scenario······ So」
For a moment, it felt as if Han Sooyoung stood before me.
As if she were speaking to me in her usual confident, firm voice.
「My only reader. This is the story of a woman who survived a ruined scenario.」
A shiver slowly crept up from the nape of my neck.
The years Han Sooyoung had lived, and
the anger, the resentment, and the waiting, all crystallized into a sentence.
「I don’t know whether you’re the right person for these ‘three methods,’ but at least one thing is certain.」
That sentence was very much like one I knew.
「You, who have read this story, will definitely survive.」
Han Sooyoung’s afterword ended there.
For a long time, I could not look away from the final period.
“Ricardo.”
I turned to find Yoo Joonghyuk looking at me.
“Did that woman also have the power to predict the future?”
“······Probably.”
[Predictive Plagiarism] had originally been the power of the 1863rd-round Han Sooyoung.
The Han Sooyoung of this round, who had written this book, had also acquired that power.
And this book was the result.
A new signpost for me, now that I had lost Ways of Survival.
[The setting takes notice of your conversation.]
[The scenario’s genre has shifted slightly toward ‘Fusion Fantasy.’]
I turned back to the first page.
Time now to read the information we needed carefully.
A sentence I had skimmed earlier suddenly caught my eye.
「P.S. This novel is a derivative work of ‘Ways of Survival’ and was written without any commercial purpose.」
A small laugh escaped me.
「Episode 1. Birth of an SSS-grade Reincarnator」
I read and reread the sentences Han Sooyoung had written with such care.
As if walking, intoxicated, into another world, I greedily savored those sentences. That was the only way I, the reader, could show respect to the author of this story.
It was good, damn it.
In places, even better than ‘Ways of Survival’.
And then, after who knew how long, I lifted my head.
Han Sooyoung had said it.
That there were three ways to clear this scenario.
「Each of the three strategies represents a genre.」
Fantasy, Romance Fantasy, and Fusion Fantasy.
「The ‘Dynastic Revolution’ route is the main plot of the ‘Fantasy’ genre. If you choose this route······.」
Every route had advantages and disadvantages. If you gained something, you lost something else.
And there were things you would lose no matter which route you chose.
For instance, the first thing we would lose was
“P-please spare me! Prince-nim! Spare me!”
Lee Hyunsung’s human rights.
“Roll left.”
“Urgh, grrrgh!”
“Roll right.”
“Prince-nim······!”
“When did I order you to talk back?”
Yoo Joonghyuk was putting Lee Hyunsung through corrective drills like a military instructor.
And I was watching.
“W-why are you making me do this? Fourth Prince-nim, please stop him!”
“Does any of this remind you of anything?”
“U-urgh······ My back hurts so much. I’m an old soldier, you know.”
To follow the routes Han Sooyoung had foreseen with [Predictive Plagiarism], we needed to restore Lee Hyunsung’s memories. And some things were remembered better by the body than the mind.
「This will probably be cruel to Lee Hyunsung, though.」
For now, we had no other way.
Her book did not record Bilston’s years from Lee Hyunsung’s perspective, either. We did not know what sort of life he had lived before the world consumed him, which limited our ways of waking him.
And how much time had passed?
“Something feels strange.”
Lee Hyunsung, his head planted against the floor, suddenly started talking nonsense.
“I’m feeling more and more at ease.”
[The character ‘Bilston’ feels severely confused.]
[The self of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ stirs.]
Yoo Joonghyuk and I looked at each other at the same time.
Normally, this much stimulus could never have awakened Lee Hyunsung’s self.
But things were a little different now.
I was here. Yoo Joonghyuk was here.
[Beings who share your Stories are nearby.]
[The bonds between Stories grow stronger!]
Three members of <Kim Dokja’s Company> were gathered here.
There was an old saying.
Three people make a tiger (三人成虎).
Get three people together, and they can make even a tiger.
We might not be able to make a tiger, but perhaps we could accomplish something else.
[Your nebula’s Stories begin resisting the ‘setting’.]
Such as calling forth memories that did not exist in this world.
[The self of the character ‘Lee Hyunsung’ slowly opens its eyes.]
Faint rays of light were flowing from Lee Hyunsung’s body.
[The Giant Story ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’ glares at you!]
Han Sooyoung had said this scenario was ultimately a world under the control of that ‘Giant Story’. If we could escape its control, perhaps recovering their selves would be possible too.
Lee Hyunsung blinked slowly, working his mouth like a babbling baby.
“······D-Dokja-ssi?”
[The setting penalizes an utterance that violates probability!]
Tzzzzzz!
“Uwaaaagh!”
Lee Hyunsung thrashed as the sparks shocked him.
I turned to see Yoo Joonghyuk getting up, ready for battle.
All the necessary preparations were complete.
Drawing the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword], Yoo Joonghyuk asked,
―Which route will we take?
―The one we always take.
Han Sooyoung was this scenario’s author.
But having an excellent author did not guarantee a work’s success.
―Let’s start clearing this scenario, Yoo Joonghyuk.
In the end, it was the ‘characters’ who completed a story, not its author.
[A new ‘Giant Story’ sprouts in your nebula.]
Erich Striker, captain of the Kaizenix Archipelago’s royal guard.
The archipelago’s undisputed strongest knight, and the king’s first sword.
It was ceaseless training, day and night, that had brought her to her present position.
Swoosh!
Erich cut again and again through the training ground’s silent night.
Drops of sweat pattered down. Watching them fall, she thought they should have been someone’s blood.
‘I let them get away. Right before Her Majesty’s eyes.’
The First Prince’s Rebellion.

Gossips were already chattering away about the audience-chamber attack two days earlier, saying whatever they pleased. Some bards were even singing songs they had composed. Most praised the first prince.
「Oh, great revolutionary Schweichen von Kaizenix」
「Behold his broad shoulders and back」

A bright streak split the training ground’s darkness. She recalled the fourth prince’s irritating face as he fled with the first. A face that would not disappear, however often she slashed through the dark.
Strangely, whenever she recalled that face, a feeling she could not quite define came over her.
The retreating backs of the first prince Schweichen, the fourth prince Ricardo, and Bilston Framer. The instant she saw those three backs, an inexplicable longing had gripped her.
Unwilling to acknowledge that feeling, Erich swung her sword.
As always, she tried to shake off her thoughts by swinging it again and again.
But it seemed tonight’s training was over.
‘An attack?’
A slender shadow flickering in the dark.
Erich immediately drew the real sword at her waist. At the slightest suspicious movement, she intended to cut the intruder down. Unexpectedly, the intruder made their presence known first.
“Put away your sword. I haven’t come to fight.”
A slender man stepped out into the faint moonlight.
Ricardo von Kaizenix, the archipelago’s fourth prince.
Erich shouted,
“Have you lost your mind? What possessed you to come here?”
“Even in a different world, you still love swords.”
Erich raised her sword, radiating menace, and the fourth prince laid his own on the ground. Her eyes narrowed.
“What are you scheming?”
“In ten minutes, the guards will rush here and surround me anyway. And with your skill, subduing me would hardly be difficult.”
“And?”
“I will surrender willingly. I mean to let you arrest me and take me to the execution ground.”
She had always known the fourth prince was not quite right in the head.
But she had not anticipated this.
He had escaped with the first prince’s help only the day before yesterday. Now he had walked back in to be executed?
Still suspicious, Erich slowly approached him.
The fourth prince really was unarmed. Without wasting the opportunity, Erich bound him.
Eyes shining innocently in the moonlight met hers.
“In return, I’d like you to listen to my story for just ten minutes.”
“Why should I?”
“It’s a dying man’s request. Refuse, and it will weigh on your conscience later.”
Erich looked down at him with a conflicted expression.
“If you mean to protest your innocence, I won’t listen.”
She knew the fourth prince was innocent.
But the archipelago had a new king now, and Erich was the captain of that king’s royal guard.
The fourth prince smiled and shook his head.
“That’s not the story I mean.”
“Then?”
“Honestly, I’ve thought about it a great deal. I have no idea what I could say to bring back the person I know.”
Bewildered by this abrupt introduction, Erich frowned.
Was this a new kind of trick?
The fourth prince’s clever way with words, which he used to seduce women, was famous throughout the archipelago.
“Long ago, there was a woman.”
Regardless, his story had begun.
“She loved kendo, and was talented enough to compete as her district’s representative.”
Along with a faint ache, an unfamiliar sensation pricked inside her head.
“With her sword, she saved her precious comrades time and again.”
Something that had vanished long ago.
“She repeatedly swung her sword against the scenarios’ injustice. She protected me with it, too.”
“What are you talking about? I am Her Majesty’s sword, and nothing else.”
The fourth prince looked up at Erich with apparent sorrow.
“You really don’t remember anything.”
That was when another voice came from the darkness.
“Prince Ricardo-nim. I would like to speak.”
Erich, who had been binding the fourth prince, started and rose. Since when had two men been standing in the dark? She growled,
“So it was a trap.”
“It is not a trap.”
The man who emerged from the darkness was Bilston Framer.
The only knight in this archipelago she respected.
“Dame Erich.”
Bilston took a step toward her. Startled, Erich warned him,
“One step closer, and I cut off the fourth prince’s head.”
This was a trap. She had to flee.
Thinking that, Erich searched for the training ground’s exit.
But something was wrong.
[Stories connected to you begin running wild in unison!]
Her body would not move, as though it had frozen solid.
[Your Stories rebel against the control of ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’!]
“We promised we wouldn’t forget.”
Bilston, looking at her with sad eyes.
No······ his name was······.
[Stories connected to you recall old memories.]
“Heewon-ssi.”
[Forgotten Stories begin their storytelling.]
In that instant, the world collapsed.
A Story spilled down and covered Erich’s memories.
The story of ten lost years.
It was the story of a time when Erich was not yet Erich, and Bilston was not yet Bilston.
Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon had come to this world exactly ten years ago.
“Hyunsung-ssi! It really is you, Hyunsung-ssi, right?”
“Oh, Heewon-ssi?”
Tzzzzzz······!
Having possessed bodies in this world around the same time, the two had fortunately recognized each other early on.
―I think we’ll have to use [Sound Transmission] here.
Bit by bit, they gathered information about this world.
That this was the final preliminary stage for entering the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’.
That <Kim Dokja’s Company> was being summoned here at different times.
And that the scenario would not begin until every assigned role was present.
―Anyway, Hyunsung-ssi, you possessed someone similar to you.
―Your role suits you very well too, Heewon-ssi.
And that, as time passed, this world would eat away at their selves.
[The Giant Story ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’ monitors your actions.]
[The world’s probability forces your assigned role upon you.]
Whenever they felt the Giant Story watching, the two had to play their roles to avoid offending it.
―It seems Sooyoung-ssi has forgotten everything. No matter what I say······.
―Will we end up like that too?
―I believe Dokja-ssi will definitely come before that happens.
They waited and waited.
―Do you think Jihye and the kids are all right?
―Those children will be fine.
Only each other to depend on in the whole world.
[The Story ‘Purest Companionship’ begins its storytelling.]
In a place where no one knew their story, they had to keep talking to preserve themselves.
Clang!
“Dame Erich! Finish him!”
“Let’s go! Sir Bilston!”
It was natural for the two to become rivals in their roles.
The more opportunities they had to stay close, the more opportunities they had to use [Sound Transmission].
―Your swordsmanship has improved a lot. You’re living up to the name ‘Steel Sword Emperor,’ aren’t you?
―When we get back, I’ll have to ask Dokja-ssi to buy me a sword.
Sound Transmissions passed between them each time their swords met.
―At this rate, you might be a swordmaster by the time Dokja-ssi gets here.
And so a year passed, then two.
Then, according to their inclinations, they joined different factions.
Lee Hyunsung, to the fourth prince Ricardo’s faction.
Jung Heewon, under the command of the ‘Black Mage’.
Different affiliations meant different surroundings.
They could no longer cross swords as often as before. More and more often, they had to live as ‘Erich Striker’ and ‘Bilston Framer’ rather than Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung.
They ate like Erich Striker and spoke like Bilston Framer. As things unlike themselves accumulated, Lee Hyunsung and Jung Heewon gradually forgot something.
Little by little, they were becoming characters of the ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’.
Once, after drinking, Jung Heewon went to Lee Hyunsung and said,
―I’m a terrible person, Hyunsung-ssi.
―Why would you say that?
―Could that be why I’m being punished?
She began to speak of things no one had mentioned before.
―The mother and daughter at Geumho Station······ Do you remember them? The ones who fought the Cheoldoo Group with us.
―······I remember. We met them in the Dark Castle too.
Lee Hyunsung recalled the mother and daughter at Geumho Station.
The mother who had fought to protect her child, and the little girl holding her mother’s hand.
The girl’s mother had died in the Dark Castle. Left alone, the girl had been entrusted to the wanderers.
―They could both have lived. If I’d realized what ‘Paradise’ really was sooner······
―It wasn’t your fault, Heewon-ssi. We couldn’t have prevented it.
―There were Stories smaller than us, weren’t there? Perhaps Stories that never even became Stories.
The drunken Jung Heewon smiled. The remnants of Stories in her hand glowed white. Every one was a story she had built. Stories made fighting great constellations as a member of <Kim Dokja’s Company>.
Jung Heewon had been proud of those stories and lived without shame.
But lately, she had begun to think a little differently.
―Maybe all the Stories we gathered were built by trampling those smaller Stories.
―Heewon-ssi.
―And now, maybe it’s our turn.
Four years passed, then five.
Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung did not give up.
―By the way, what were Yoosung and Gilyoung’s surnames?
―Lee Yoosung and Shin Gilyoung······ weren’t they?
―Something feels wrong······.
Their memories faded little by little.
And so six years had passed.
―Where do you think Dokja-ssi is, and what is he doing?
―I think he’ll come before the year is out.
Seven years had passed.
―Seven years of unpaid wages. Isn’t this company completely exploitative?
―Let’s make sure we form a union later.
―Let’s do that. Don’t forget.
Their promise to meet and talk at least once a week became once a month, then once every two months.
More and more often, they met without saying anything at all.
Then one day in the eighth year, Jung Heewon asked in a dazed voice,
―Weren’t we waiting for something?
Lee Hyunsung could not answer.
―You know, Hyunsung-ssi. If I forget you.
―I’ll remember.
―Kill me.
And that was Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung’s last meeting.
Not long after, the ‘Black Mage’ started a revolution.
And Lee Hyunsung found himself facing Jung Heewon as he fought for the old dynasty.
―Heewon-ssi.
Their swords clashed again and again in the air.
Amid the dazzling swordlight, wounds multiplied on Lee Hyunsung’s body. Trajectories unmistakably different from those in their sparring matches. Sword strikes carrying a clear intent to kill him.
―Heewon-ssi.
Despite repeated uses of [Sound Transmission], Jung Heewon did not answer. Her silence was the answer.
As though she had been holding back until now, Erich’s merciless sword cut through Lee Hyunsung. His vision fading into darkness. Staggering, he approached the Jung Heewon he remembered.
One step, then two.
At last, looking into her eyes up close, Lee Hyunsung said for the first time what he had long been unable to say, and would never be able to say again.
―I like you, Heewon-ssi.
[The Story ‘Purest Companionship’ finishes its storytelling.]
I read the Story in silence.
Some sentences were quietly sorrowful. Some hurt as if my heart were being torn apart.
[The self of the character ‘Jung Heewon’ gradually awakens.]
Faint light drifted over Bilston and Erich’s bodies. I could feel their two souls resonating with the Story.
Lee Hyunsung, lying there smiling.
I looked down at his face for a moment, then muttered,
“I think we’ll have to change the company regulations······.”
Anyway, that accomplished our second objective. Next was······.
“Over there!”
“Dame Erich is in danger!”
Yoo Joonghyuk lifted the fallen Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung, one in each arm. But before we could escape, the training ground’s doors opened and the royal guard burst in.
And the royal guard were not alone.
Someone approached through the ranks of guards.
「The Kaizenix Archipelago’s first Triple Master」
「A genius who became a swordmaster at eighteen」
「The youngest ninth-circle archmage」
「The archipelago’s king, who commands an evil black dragon」
At present, no one in the Kaizenix Archipelago could match that person.
The king, wearing a silver crown, smiled quietly.
“You dare try to steal my knight?”
The royal guards all knelt before her.
His expression hardening, Yoo Joonghyuk sent a message.
―This was not the plan.
―All the better.
Our next target was Han Sooyoung anyway.
Four members of <Kim Dokja’s Company> here.
A nebula’s Stories grew stronger as more of its members gathered.
Looking at the king’s face, I spoke.
“Your Majesty, we haven’t come to fight.”
Somewhere inside that king, Han Sooyoung’s self must be asleep.
I had to get it back from that character.
And now, using our Stories······.
“I know. You must have come to tell me a story.”
I looked at her in surprise.
[The Giant Story ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’ scoffs at you.]
“Why so surprised? I, too, love stories. But I prefer telling them to listening. So open your ears and listen carefully, Ricardo von Kaizenix.”
Spreading her arms wide, the king smiled at me.
“No, Kim Dokja, the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’”
I looked at the king with Han Sooyoung’s face.
That was definitely not Han Sooyoung.
Then how on earth did she know my name?
The king was still smiling.
“You must wonder how I know your name.”

The king was a character in this world, a being who merely acted according to the laws of the ‘Giant Story’. It should have been impossible for such a being to recognize me as ‘Kim Dokja’ rather than ‘Ricardo’.
Even though she spoke of things outside the world, probability sparks did not suppress her.
[The setting considers the possibility of expanding its genre.]
[The Giant Story ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’ tacitly permits the situation.]
[Probability restrictions on certain utterances are relaxed.]
[Meta-statements about the setting are permitted!]
I studied the king for a moment, then activated a skill.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
<Character Information>
Name: ???
Age: 50
Overall Evaluation: This person harbors hatred toward you.
The king’s information still did not appear.
At first I had thought Han Sooyoung was the reason. Since she was not registered in Character List, her possession had made even the information about her host, the king, uncertain.
But what if that was not it?
“Are you Han Sooyoung?”
“I was once called by that name.”
“What does that mean?”
Blinking slowly, the king continued her story.
“Do you know the story of a woman who endured decades clinging to a vain hope?”
“I know the story of a similar man very well.”
It was Yoo Joonghyuk who said that, drawing the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
The king smiled and said,
“Poor beloved, you have come to find your grave.”
“Our engagement was broken. Call me that again, and I’ll take your head.”
Almost simultaneously, the two vanished.

They collided with a deafening explosion. The training ground’s ceiling broke apart and flew skyward. Sword winds and magic waves clashed, forming a vortex in the sky. At a glance, it looked evenly matched. The details told a different story.
After ten or so exchanges in a matter of moments, Yoo Joonghyuk had a minor wound on his left arm. But the king did not have so much as a scratch.
Yoo Joonghyuk was being pushed back.
Even Yoo Joonghyuk, powerful as he was, could not overcome this world’s king.
An aura of [Black Flame], Han Sooyoung’s specialty, was even rising from the king’s left arm.
“Dokja-ssi! Get back!”
Lee Hyunsung protected me from the charging guards.
“······Dokja-ssi?”
Jung Heewon seemed to be barely regaining consciousness too. But I had no time to attend to them.
As time passed, the previously even battle turned sharply against Yoo Joonghyuk.
After all, that host body was a ‘Triple Master’, no less.
“Han Sooyoung! Wake up!”
Without hesitation, I drew on the power of a ‘Giant Story’.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm’s Spring’ begins its story.]
The Story I hurled into the air with all my strength briefly interrupted the battle.
I seized the opening and leaped into the fray.
The king smiled and spread her arms.
“Demon King of Salvation. The woman you seek died long ago.”
“Bullshit. Han Sooyoung doesn’t talk like that.”
“Do you know what fifty years mean to a human being?”
I did not.
I had never lived that long.
[The Giant Story ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’ begins its storytelling.]
The world stirred, and images of Han Sooyoung’s life here appeared in the air.
It was Han Sooyoung’s Story.
The history of her life in this world.
More precisely, the history that Han Sooyoung’s host, ‘Yuri di Aristel’, had to endure.
「The beautiful daughter of a count」
「A daughter raised solely to become queen」
「“You will enter the royal palace when you turn eighteen.”」
Among the jumble of sentences, I saw the Han Sooyoung I knew.
「“Fine, then. Shall I become a swordmaster by eighteen?”」
Han Sooyoung, fighting the world. Han Sooyoung, living here with a face I clearly recognized.
Han Sooyoung, who had lived through this world wearing expressions I did not know.
「“Why is a girl handling a sword?”」
「“Magic is nothing but sleight of hand.”」
Some clichés used the excuse of being clichés to shackle their characters.
And the Han Sooyoung I knew hated clichés more than anyone.
「“Fuck, fine, I’ll get married! If there’s a bastard stronger than me, I’ll marry him!”」
Countless men stepped forward to claim the count’s beautiful daughter.
Among them were knights of the archipelago and famous magicians.
Han Sooyoung grew stronger so she could defeat the suitors with her own hands.
After grueling training, she became a swordmaster.
A ninth-circle archmage.
And a master of terror who wielded an evil dragon’s power.
The power of a swordmaster made her body youthful, while the aura of evil black flame heightened her mystique.
Paradoxically, the stronger she became, the more the world desired her.
